title: The Majority Element

concept.title: Count until one value passes half
body: A **majority element** occurs more than `n / 2` times. If you count the occurrences in a map, you can stop as soon as one counter exceeds `n / 2`: such a value is unique, because two different values cannot both have more than half of the elements.
There is a clever O(1)-memory method (Boyer-Moore voting), but counting is simple and works when you also want to know the counts, or when no majority is guaranteed.

statement: An array of `n` integers contains a value that occurs more than `n / 2` times (the majority element). Print it.
hints: Count the occurrences of every value.
The majority element has a count larger than n / 2.
You can stop at the first counter that passes n / 2.

explanation: Two different values cannot each have more than half of the elements, so the first counter above `n / 2` is the majority element.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {}
answer = None
for x in a:
    count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
    if count[x] * 2 > n:
        answer = x
        break
print(answer)
